text:
In this experiment you will see piles of bricks stacked on a table like the example image below. Your task is to judge whether the white brick would fall off either side of the table if the black brick wasn't there. Note that all bricks have the same physical properties; they are simply colored differently.

In the original study, participants first gained experience with the physical properties of the objects by seeing bricks fall on the table. Before you begin, please answer a few questions to confirm your understanding of the task.

You will then make judgments for 43 different piles of bricks. Note that each pile is stable. The original study also included catch trials throughout the experiment and an attention check at the end.

In this experiment you will see piles of bricks stacked on table like shown in the example image below. Your task is to judge how responsible the black brick is for the white brick staying on the table. Note that all bricks have the same physical properties; they are simply colored differently.

Before you begin, please answer a few questions to confirm your understanding of the task.

You will then make judgments for 43 different piles of bricks. Note that each pile is stable.
